::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 4th [1893?]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MSS. Autogr. b.9 pp 460-1[^1]
:::

Dear Madam
I am much obliged for your offer but I am afraid you have been forestalled as we have had two papers upon [Palermo](other_books/otherbook_682.qmd) and [Taormina](other_books/otherbook_681.qmd) by Miss [Florence Freeman](people/person_524.qmd), written and we could hardly go over the same ground[^2]

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: A tiny piece from an envelope is pasted in with the address ‘The Revd/ J.J. Stone/ Windsor’.  The recipient was perhaps a member of his household, or the letter may not belong to it.
[^2]: Florence Freeman, 'Taormina and its Neighbourhood' *MP* 3s 2  (December 1891), 617-29; and 'Palermo and its Neighbourhood' *MP* 3s 6 (September 1893), 296-310.
